stem: Let \(f(x) = 4x^{3} + \dfrac{6}{x}\), for \(x \ne 0\).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find \(f'(x)\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the gradient of the graph of \(f\) at the point where \(x = 2\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Show that \(f\) is decreasing at \(x = 0.5\).

idea: Write \(\dfrac{6}{x}\) as a power of \(x\), \(6x^{-1}\), before differentiating. The derivative of \(ax^{n}\) is \(nax^{n-1}\). A function is decreasing at a point where its derivative is negative.

solution.label: c
steps: The gradient is negative, so \(f\) is decreasing at \(x = 0.5\).

stem: The plug is pulled out of a full bath. The volume of water left in the bath, \(V\) litres, \(t\) minutes later is modelled by \[V(t) = 90 - 12t + 0.4t^{2}, \quad 0 \le t \le 15.\] The bath is empty after 15 minutes.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write down the volume of water in the bath when the plug is pulled out.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t}\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the value of \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t}\) when \(t = 5\), and explain what it means in this context.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the time at which the water is draining out at 4 litres per minute.

idea: The derivative \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t}\) is the rate of change of the volume, in litres per minute. A negative rate means the volume is going down.

solution.label: c
solution.answer: \(-8\): 5 minutes after the plug is pulled, the volume is going down at 8 litres per minute

solution.label: d
steps: Draining at 4 litres per minute means \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t} = -4\).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find \(f'(x)\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Solve \(f'(x) = 0\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Write down the values of \(x\) for which \(f\) is decreasing.

idea: \(f\) is decreasing where \(f'(x) < 0\). The solutions of \(f'(x) = 0\) split the number line into intervals, and the sign of \(f'\) can be tested at one value in each interval.

solution.label: a
steps: Differentiate term by term; the constant 1 has derivative 0.

solution.label: c
steps: Test a value in each interval: \(f'(-3) = 15 > 0\), \(f'(0) = -12 < 0\) and \(f'(3) = 15 > 0\).
So \(f'(x) < 0\) only between the two solutions.

stem: The price, \(P\) dollars, of one share in a new company \(t\) days after the shares first go on sale is modelled by \[P(t) = 10 + 2.4t - 0.02t^{2}, \quad 0 \le t \le 100.\]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}P}{\mathrm{d}t}\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the rate at which the price is changing on day 20. Give the units of your answer.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the day on which the price stops rising.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the highest price of a share.

idea: The price is rising while \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}P}{\mathrm{d}t} > 0\) and falling while \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}P}{\mathrm{d}t} < 0\). It stops rising where the rate of change is zero, and that is where the price is highest.

solution.label: b
solution.answer: 1.6 dollars per day (the price is rising)

solution.label: c
steps: \(2.4 - 0.04t = 0\), so \(t = 60\). Before day 60 the rate is positive, and after it the rate is negative.

stem: A curve has equation \(y = ax^{2} + \dfrac{b}{x}\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are constants and \(x \ne 0\). The gradient of the curve is 6 at the point where \(x = 1\), and 15.5 at the point where \(x = 2\).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\) in terms of \(a\), \(b\) and \(x\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write down two equations in \(a\) and \(b\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the value of \(a\) and the value of \(b\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the gradient of the curve at the point where \(x = -1\).

idea: Each piece of information about a gradient gives an equation: substitute the value of \(x\) into \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\) and set it equal to the gradient. Two equations are enough to find two unknowns.

solution.label: c
steps: Solve the two equations together, for example with the calculator's equation solver, or substitute \(b = 2a - 6\) into the second equation: \(4a - 0.5a + 1.5 = 15.5\), so \(3.5a = 14\).

stem: The number of people inside a shopping centre, \(N\) hundred, \(t\) hours after it opens at 10 am is modelled by \[N(t) = 0.5t^{3} - 6t^{2} + 18t + 4, \quad 0 \le t \le 8.\]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write down the number of people inside the shopping centre when it opens.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find \(N'(t)\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the rate at which the number of people is changing at 11 am, and explain what it means in this context.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the two times of day at which the number of people in the shopping centre is not changing.

idea: \(N\) is measured in hundreds of people, so \(N'(t)\) is in hundreds of people per hour. A time of day is found by adding the value of \(t\) to the opening time.

solution.label: c
solution.answer: 7.5: at 11 am the number of people is going up at 750 people per hour

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find \(f'(x)\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that \(f\) is decreasing for \(0 < x < 2\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the value of \(x\) at which the gradient of the graph of \(f\) is 6.

idea: Write \(f'(x)\) as a single fraction to see when it is negative. An equation such as \(f'(x) = 6\) that does not rearrange neatly can be solved with the calculator.

solution.label: b
solution.answer: \(f'(x) < 0\) for \(0 < x < 2\), so \(f\) is decreasing there

stem: Let \(f(x) = x^{3} + kx^{2} + 12x\), where \(k\) is a constant.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find \(f'(x)\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: The graph of \(f\) has a stationary point at \(x = 2\). Find the value of \(k\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: For this value of \(k\), show that \(f'(x) = 3(x - 2)^{2}\), and hence explain why \(f\) is never decreasing.

parts.label: d
parts.text: For a different curve, \(k = -9\). Find the values of \(x\) for which this function is decreasing.

idea: A stationary point is where \(f'(x) = 0\). A square is never negative, so a derivative of the form \(3(x - 2)^{2}\) is never negative. Where \(f'(x)\) is a quadratic, \(f\) decreases between its two zeros if it has two.

solution.label: c
steps: \((x - 2)^{2} \ge 0\) for every \(x\), so \(f'(x) \ge 0\): the gradient is never negative. It is zero only at \(x = 2\).
solution.answer: \(f'(x) = 3(x - 2)^{2} \ge 0\) for all \(x\), so \(f\) is never decreasing

solution.label: d
steps: \(f'(x) = 3x^{2} - 18x + 12\). Its zeros, from the calculator, are \(x = 0.7639\ldots\) and \(x = 5.236\ldots\)
Between them \(f'(x)\) is negative, for example \(f'(1) = -3\).

stem: A train leaves a station and travels along a straight track to the next station. Its distance from the first station, \(s\) metres, \(t\) seconds after it starts is modelled by \[s(t) = 0.3t^{2} - 0.001t^{3}, \quad 0 \le t \le 200.\] The speed of the train, \(v\) metres per second, is the rate of change of \(s\).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find an expression for \(v\) in terms of \(t\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed of the train 50 seconds after it starts.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the two times at which the speed of the train is 27 metres per second.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the greatest speed of the train.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Show that the train is at rest when \(t = 200\), and find the distance between the two stations.

idea: The speed is the derivative of the distance, \(v = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}s}{\mathrm{d}t}\). The greatest speed is at a stationary point of \(v\), where its own rate of change is zero.

solution.label: c
steps: Solve \(0.6t - 0.003t^{2} = 27\) with the calculator: \(t = 68.37\ldots\) or \(t = 131.6\ldots\) Both are in the interval \(0 \le t \le 200\).

solution.label: d
steps: The rate of change of \(v\) is \(0.6 - 0.006t\), which is zero when \(t = 100\).
\(v(100) = 60 - 30 = 30\). (The calculator's maximum of the graph of \(v\) gives the same.)

stem: A curve has equation \(y = x^{2} - 4x + 7\).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point where \(x = 3\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the point where this tangent crosses the \(x\)-axis.

idea: The tangent at a point touches the curve there and has the same gradient as the curve. Find the point and the gradient, then use \(y - y_{1} = m(x - x_{1})\).

stem: Let \(f(x) = 2x^{3} - x\). The point \(\mathrm{P}(1, 1)\) lies on the graph of \(f\).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find \(f'(x)\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the gradient of the normal to the graph of \(f\) at P.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the equation of the normal at P. Give your answer in the form \(ax + by + d = 0\), where \(a\), \(b\) and \(d\) are integers.

idea: The normal at a point is perpendicular to the tangent there. If the tangent has gradient \(m\), the normal has gradient \(-\dfrac{1}{m}\).

solution.label: b
steps: The tangent at P has gradient \(f'(1) = 5\). The normal's gradient is \(-\dfrac{1}{5}\).

stem: Let \(f(x) = \dfrac{6}{x} + x\), for \(x > 0\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find \(f'(x)\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the equation of the tangent to the graph of \(f\) at the point where \(x = 2\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: The tangent crosses the \(x\)-axis at A and the \(y\)-axis at B. Find the area of the triangle OAB, where O is the origin.

idea: Find the point of contact and the gradient there, then write the equation of the line. A line crosses the \(x\)-axis where \(y = 0\) and the \(y\)-axis where \(x = 0\).

solution.label: d
steps: The triangle has a right angle at O: area \(= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 12 \times 6\).

stem: The line \(y = 5x + c\) is a tangent to the curve \(y = x^{2} + x + 7\).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the point where the line touches the curve.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the value of \(c\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the equation of the normal to the curve at the same point.

idea: Where a line touches a curve, the curve's gradient equals the gradient of the line. That fixes the point, and the point must lie on the line too.

solution.label: b
steps: The line has gradient 5: \(2x + 1 = 5\), so \(x = 2\). Then \(y = 4 + 2 + 7 = 13\).

solution.label: c
steps: The point lies on the line: \(13 = 5 \times 2 + c\).

stem: The side view of a mountain-bike trail down a slope is modelled by \[y = 0.002x^{3} - 0.06x^{2} + 10, \quad 0 \le x \le 20,\] where \(x\) metres is the horizontal distance from the top of the trail and \(y\) metres is the height above the bottom of the valley.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the gradient of the trail at the point where \(x = 5\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the equation of the tangent to the trail at the point where \(x = 5\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the angle between the trail and the horizontal at the point where \(x = 5\).

idea: The gradient at a point is the gradient of the tangent there. A gradient \(m\) is the tangent of the angle the line makes with the horizontal, so the angle is \(\tan^{-1}\) of the size of the gradient.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find \(f'(x)\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the tangent to the graph of \(f\) at the point where \(x = 2\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the equation of the normal to the graph of \(f\) at the same point.

parts.label: d
parts.text: The tangent crosses the \(x\)-axis at A and the normal crosses the \(x\)-axis at B. Find the distance AB.

idea: Write \(f(x) = 8x^{-2}\) to differentiate. The tangent and the normal pass through the same point; their gradients multiply to \(-1\).

stem: A bend on a go-kart track follows the curve \(y = 0.02x^{2}\), for \(-50 \le x \le 50\), where \(x\) and \(y\) are in metres. A marshal's hut stands at H\((40, 20)\), as shown in the diagram.
A kart skids at the point \(\mathrm{P}(a, 0.02a^{2})\) on the track, and leaves it in a straight line along the tangent to the curve at P. It travels towards the hut.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the tangent to the curve at P has equation \(y = 0.04ax - 0.02a^{2}\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: The tangent at P passes through H. Find the value of \(a\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the distance from P to the hut.

idea: The tangent at a general point P has a gradient that depends on \(a\). Making the tangent pass through H gives an equation in \(a\); only a solution that lies on the bend, \(-50 \le a \le 50\), fits the situation.

solution.label: c
steps: The calculator gives \(a = 15.50\ldots\) or \(a = 64.49\ldots\) The second value is not on the bend, because the bend ends at \(x = 50\).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find \(f'(x)\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Solve \(f'(x) = 0\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the two stationary points of the graph of \(f\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: State which of the two points is a local maximum. Give a reason.

idea: Stationary points are where the gradient is zero. To find their coordinates, substitute each \(x\)-value back into \(f(x)\), not into \(f'(x)\).

solution.label: d
steps: \(f'(-3) = 36 > 0\) and \(f'(0) = -36 < 0\): the gradient changes from positive to negative at \(x = -2\).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find \(f'(x)\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the graph of \(f\) has a stationary point at \(x = 2\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the coordinates of all three stationary points of the graph of \(f\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: State the nature of each stationary point.

idea: Set \(f'(x) = 0\) and solve; a cubic derivative can have three solutions. The nature of each point comes from the sign of \(f'(x)\) on either side, or from the shape of the graph on the calculator.

solution.label: b
solution.answer: \(f'(2) = 0\), so there is a stationary point at \(x = 2\)

solution.label: d
steps: \(f'(-1) = 12 > 0\) and \(f'(1) = -12 < 0\), so the gradient goes from positive to negative at \(x = 0\). On the outside, \(f'(-3) = -60 < 0\) and \(f'(3) = 60 > 0\).
solution.answer: \((0, 3)\) is a local maximum; \((2, -13)\) and \((-2, -13)\) are local minima

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find \(f'(x)\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the graph of \(f\) has a stationary point where \(x = \sqrt[3]{50}\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the coordinates of this stationary point.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Determine whether this point is a local maximum or a local minimum.

idea: Write \(\dfrac{50}{x^{2}}\) as \(50x^{-2}\). At the stationary point \(f'(x) = 0\); multiply through by \(x^{3}\) to clear the fraction. Test the sign of \(f'(x)\) on each side to decide its nature.

solution.label: d
steps: \(f'(3) = 2 - 3.70\ldots < 0\) and \(f'(4) = 2 - 1.5625 > 0\): the gradient goes from negative to positive.

stem: The temperature inside a garden shed, \(T\) °C, \(t\) hours after midnight is modelled by \[T(t) = -0.02t^{3} + 0.6t^{2} - 3.6t + 22, \quad 0 \le t \le 20.\]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find \(T'(t)\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the values of \(t\) at which \(T'(t) = 0\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the highest temperature in the shed during this time.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the values of \(t\) for which the temperature is rising.

idea: The temperature has a local minimum and a local maximum where \(T'(t) = 0\). The highest value over the whole interval could also be at an end point, so check \(T(0)\) and \(T(20)\) as well.

solution.label: b
steps: Solve with the calculator, or divide by \(-0.06\): \(t^{2} - 20t + 60 = 0\).

solution.label: c
steps: \(T(16.32\ldots) = 36.11\ldots\) This is a local maximum, because \(T'\) changes from positive to negative there.
Check the end points: \(T(0) = 22\) and \(T(20) = 30\), both lower.

solution.label: d
steps: \(T'(t) > 0\) between the two solutions, for example \(T'(10) = 2.4\).

stem: Let \(f(x) = x^{2} - 4x + \dfrac{12}{x}\), for \(x > 0\). The graph of \(f\) has one stationary point, which is a local minimum.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find \(f'(x)\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use your calculator to find the \(x\)-coordinate of the stationary point.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the minimum value of \(f(x)\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: Hence explain why \(f(x) > 0\) for all \(x > 0\).

idea: The equation \(f'(x) = 0\) is a cubic once the fraction is cleared, so solve it with the calculator. The minimum value is \(f\) at that point, and every other value of \(f\) is larger.

solution.label: d
steps: The smallest value of \(f(x)\) for \(x > 0\) is 0.925, which is positive.
solution.answer: Every value of \(f(x)\) is at least 0.925, so it is positive

stem: Let \(f(x) = x^{3} - 3kx^{2} + 4\), where \(k\) is a positive constant.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find \(f'(x)\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the graph of \(f\) has stationary points at \(x = 0\) and \(x = 2k\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: The stationary point at \(x = 2k\) is a local minimum, and it lies on the \(x\)-axis. Find the value of \(k\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: For this value of \(k\), find the other point where the graph of \(f\) meets the \(x\)-axis.

idea: Factorise \(f'(x)\) to find the stationary points in terms of \(k\). A point on the \(x\)-axis has \(y = 0\), which gives an equation for \(k\).

solution.label: a
steps: Differentiate term by term; \(k\) is a constant.

solution.label: d
steps: \(f(x) = x^{3} - 3x^{2} + 4\). Solve \(f(x) = 0\) with the calculator: \(x = -1\) or \(x = 2\). The point at \(x = 2\) is the minimum.

stem: The height of a survey drone above the ground, \(h\) metres, \(t\) minutes after take-off is modelled by \[h(t) = t^{3} - 15t^{2} + 63t, \quad 0 \le t \le 10.\]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find \(h'(t)\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the values of \(t\) at which \(h'(t) = 0\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the height of the drone at each of these times, and state which is a local maximum.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the greatest height of the drone during the 10 minutes. Explain your answer.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Write down the values of \(t\) for which the drone is descending.

idea: A local maximum is only the highest point nearby. Over a closed interval, the greatest value is either a local maximum or a value at one of the end points, so compare all of them.

solution.label: c
steps: \(h'(2) = 15 > 0\) and \(h'(4) = -9 < 0\), so \(t = 3\) gives a local maximum; \(t = 7\) gives a local minimum.
solution.answer: 81 m at \(t = 3\) (local maximum) and 49 m at \(t = 7\) (local minimum)

solution.label: d
steps: Compare the local maximum with the end points: \(h(0) = 0\) and \(h(10) = 1000 - 1500 + 630 = 130\).
After \(t = 7\) the drone climbs again and passes 81 m.
solution.answer: 130 m, at \(t = 10\): higher than the local maximum of 81 m

solution.label: e
steps: The drone descends where \(h'(t) < 0\), which is between the two solutions.

stem: A climbing centre sells weekly passes. When the price of a pass is \(p\) dollars, the number of passes sold each week is \(900 - 30p\), for \(5 \le p \le 25\).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the weekly income from the passes, \(R\) dollars, is given by \(R = 900p - 30p^{2}\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}R}{\mathrm{d}p}\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the price that gives the greatest weekly income.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the greatest weekly income.

idea: Income is price times the number sold. The greatest income is at a stationary point of \(R\), where \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}R}{\mathrm{d}p} = 0\).

solution.label: c
steps: \(900 - 60p = 0\), so \(p = 15\). The gradient is positive below 15 and negative above it, so this is a maximum.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that \(h = \dfrac{0.144}{x^{2}}\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the area of wood needed, \(A\) m\(^{2}\), is given by \(A = 2x^{2} + \dfrac{0.864}{x}\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}A}{\mathrm{d}x}\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the dimensions of the planter that needs the least wood, and the area of wood it needs.

idea: Use the volume to write \(h\) in terms of \(x\). The wood is the base and four sides (no top). Then the area depends on \(x\) only, and its least value is where \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}A}{\mathrm{d}x} = 0\).

solution.label: b
steps: Base: \(2x^{2}\). Two sides of \(x \times h\) and two of \(2x \times h\): \(2xh + 4xh = 6xh\).

parts.text: Show that the area of the rectangle, \(R\) m\(^{2}\), is given by \(R = 100r - 2\pi r^{2}\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the value of \(r\) that makes \(R\) as large as possible.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the largest area of the rectangle, and the value of \(x\) that gives it.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Show that, for these dimensions, the rectangle is \(\dfrac{2}{3}\) of the whole area of the rink.

steps: \(100 - 4\pi r = 0\), so \(r = \dfrac{25}{\pi} = 7.957\ldots\) The gradient goes from positive to negative, so this is a maximum.

steps: The two semicircles make a circle of area \(\pi r^{2} = \pi \times \dfrac{625}{\pi^{2}} = \dfrac{625}{\pi} = 198.9\ldots\)

parts.label: a

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the average cost per T-shirt, \(A\) dollars, is given by \(A(x) = 0.02x + 4 + \dfrac{800}{x}\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find \(A'(x)\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the number of T-shirts in an order that makes the average cost as small as possible, and find this smallest average cost.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Show that, for this order size, \(C'(x)\) is equal to the average cost.

idea: The average cost is the total cost divided by the number made. A large order spreads the fixed cost of $800, but the \(0.02x^{2}\) term grows; the best order size is where \(A'(x) = 0\).

solution.label: d
steps: \(0.02 - \dfrac{800}{x^{2}} = 0\), so \(x^{2} = 40\,000\) and \(x = 200\). The gradient goes from negative to positive, so this is a minimum.
solution.answer: 200 T-shirts, with an average cost of $12

idea: The area between a curve and the \(x\)-axis, where the curve is above the axis, is the definite integral between the two \(x\)-values. Region B sits on top of region A inside a rectangle, so it is the rectangle minus A.

parts.label: a

parts.label: b

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the rate of charging when \(t = 10\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the percentage of the 10-minute increase that takes place in the first 5 minutes.

idea: Integrating a rate over a time interval gives the total change over that interval. Add the change to the starting value to get the new value.

solution.label: a
steps: The increase is the area under the graph of the rate.

stem: The diagram shows part of the graph of \(y = \dfrac{8}{x^{2}} + 1\), for \(x > 0\). The shaded region is bounded by the curve, the \(x\)-axis and the lines \(x = 1\) and \(x = 4\).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write down an integral that gives the area of the shaded region.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that \(\displaystyle\int \left(\dfrac{8}{x^{2}} + 1\right)\mathrm{d}x = -\dfrac{8}{x} + x + C\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the area of the shaded region.

parts.label: d
parts.text: The line \(x = k\), where \(1 < k < 4\), divides the shaded region into two parts. The part between \(x = 1\) and \(x = k\) has area 5. Find the value of \(k\).

idea: Write \(\dfrac{8}{x^{2}}\) as \(8x^{-2}\) before integrating. With an unknown limit \(k\), the definite integral is an expression in \(k\), and setting it equal to the area gives an equation.

solution.label: a
steps: The curve is above the \(x\)-axis for \(x > 0\).

solution.label: d
steps: So \(k - \dfrac{8}{k} + 2 = 0\). Multiply by \(k\): \(k^{2} + 2k - 8 = 0\), so \((k + 4)(k - 2) = 0\). Only \(k = 2\) lies between 1 and 4.

stem: When the gates of a sports stand open, 500 people (staff and season-ticket holders) are already inside. Spectators then come in at a rate of \(R\) people per minute, where \[R(t) = 40 + 12t - 0.6t^{2}, \quad 0 \le t \le 20,\] and \(t\) is the time in minutes since the gates opened.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find an expression for the number of people inside the stand, \(N\), after \(t\) minutes.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the number of people inside after 10 minutes.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The stand holds 2000 people. Find the time at which it becomes full.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the greatest rate at which spectators come in.

idea: \(R\) is the rate of change of \(N\), so \(N\) is found by integrating \(R\). The 500 people inside at the start fix the constant of integration.

solution.label: c
steps: Solve \(500 + 40t + 6t^{2} - 0.2t^{3} = 2000\) with the calculator, for \(0 \le t \le 20\): \(t = 18.03\ldots\)

solution.label: d
steps: \(R'(t) = 12 - 1.2t = 0\) when \(t = 10\). The gradient of \(R\) changes from positive to negative there.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find \(f(x)\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the height of the bottom end of the slide, where \(x = 10\).

parts.label: c

parts.label: e

idea: Integrate the gradient to get the curve, and use the top of the slide to find the constant. The gradient is itself a function of \(x\), so its most negative value is at a stationary point of \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\).

solution.label: c
solution.answer: The gradient is 0 at \(x = 10\), so the slide is horizontal there

solution.label: d
steps: The rate of change of the gradient is \(0.024x - 0.12\), which is zero at \(x = 5\).
Gradient at \(x = 5\): \(0.3 - 0.6 = -0.3\). (The calculator's minimum of the graph of \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\) gives the same.)

stem: The diagram shows the curve \(y = x^{2} - 4x + 6\) and the line \(y = 6\). The shaded region is enclosed by the curve and the line.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the \(x\)-coordinates of the points where the curve meets the line.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of the region between the curve and the \(x\)-axis, from \(x = 0\) to \(x = 4\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence find the area of the shaded region.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Explain why the line \(x = 2\) divides the shaded region into two parts of equal area.

idea: The shaded region is what is left when the area under the curve is taken away from the rectangle under the line. A parabola is symmetrical about the vertical line through its vertex.

solution.label: c
steps: The rectangle under the line from \(x = 0\) to \(x = 4\) has area \(4 \times 6 = 24\).

solution.label: d
steps: The vertex of the parabola is at \(x = 2\) (where \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 2x - 4 = 0\)), and the parabola is symmetrical about this line. The line \(y = 6\) is horizontal, so the region is symmetrical too.
solution.answer: The region is symmetrical about \(x = 2\), the axis of symmetry of the parabola

stem: A surfboard is 1.8 m long. Its width is measured every 0.3 m along its length. One width, \(k\) m, has been smudged.

\[\def\arraystretch{1.4}\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline \text{Distance (m)} & \text{Width (m)} \\ \hline 0 & 0 \\ \hline 0.3 & 0.32 \\ \hline 0.6 & 0.46 \\ \hline 0.9 & k \\ \hline 1.2 & 0.48 \\ \hline 1.5 & 0.38 \\ \hline 1.8 & 0 \\ \hline \end{array}\]
The trapezoidal rule with these widths gives an estimate of 0.663 m\(^{2}\) for the area of the top of the board.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of \(k\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: The designer wants a board of the same length with an area of 0.700 m\(^{2}\). She multiplies every width by the same factor \(s\). Find \(s\), using the trapezoidal rule.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the new width at 0.9 m, to the nearest centimetre.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Another designer models the width of the original board by \(w(x) = 0.7x(1.8 - x)\), where \(x\) m is the distance along the board. Find the area of the board given by this model.

idea: Write the trapezoidal rule with \(k\) in it, and solve the equation. Multiplying every width by \(s\) multiplies the trapezoidal estimate by \(s\) too.

stem: Let \(f(x) = x^{2} + k\), where \(k\) is a constant. The trapezoidal rule with 4 strips of equal width is used to estimate \(\displaystyle\int_{0}^{8} f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x\). The estimate is 200.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the trapezoidal estimate is \(176 + 8k\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of \(k\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the exact value of \(\displaystyle\int_{0}^{8} f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x\) for this value of \(k\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: Show that, for every value of \(k\), the trapezoidal estimate is larger than the exact value by the same amount, and find this amount.

idea: Four strips from 0 to 8 have width 2, so the rule uses \(f(0)\), \(f(2)\), \(f(4)\), \(f(6)\) and \(f(8)\). Adding \(k\) raises the curve and every trapezium by the same height, so it adds the same area to both.

solution.label: d
steps: For any \(k\), the exact value is \(\left[\dfrac{x^{3}}{3} + kx\right]_{0}^{8} = \dfrac{512}{3} + 8k\).
solution.answer: The estimate is always \(\dfrac{16}{3} = 5.33\) too large

stem: This question looks at how the error in the trapezoidal rule changes with the number of strips, for \(\displaystyle I = \int_{0}^{2} x^{3}\,\mathrm{d}x\).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the trapezoidal rule with 2 strips to estimate \(I\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use the trapezoidal rule with 4 strips to estimate \(I\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the exact value of \(I\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: With 8 strips, the trapezoidal estimate is 4.0625. Find the error of each of the three estimates, and describe the pattern.

parts.label: e
parts.text: The error with \(n\) strips follows the formula \(\dfrac{4}{n^{2}}\). Find the smallest number of strips for which the error is less than 0.01.

idea: The error is the estimate minus the exact value. Doubling the number of strips halves their width; look at what happens to the error each time.

solution.label: d
solution.answer: 1, 0.25 and 0.0625: each time the number of strips doubles, the error is divided by 4

solution.label: e
steps: \(\dfrac{4}{n^{2}} < 0.01\), so \(n^{2} > 400\) and \(n > 20\). With 20 strips the error is exactly 0.01, which is not less than 0.01.
